Okay, so this week the rover team spent way more time on one rock than we planned, and honestly, nobody minds. It's about the size of a loaf of bread, kind of reddish with these little pits all over it, and when we first saw it in the navigation images somebody on the team joked that it looked like a sponge. We drove up next to it on Tuesday and took close-up pictures with the arm camera. Then we used the little brush to clear off the dust so the spectrometer could get a clean reading. The results came back yesterday and they're interesting: more iron than the rocks around it, and a bit of sulfur too. We're not going to claim we know what that means yet. That takes a lot of arguing around a table. But it's a good reason to stay put for another day or two before we keep heading toward the ridge.
